record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.context_brief: Producing hard families from small hard functions
record.original_question: Suppose one starts with a Boolean function on a constant number of inputs that already has high circuit complexity. Can one systematically turn it into a family of n-input Boolean functions whose circuit complexity stays high, rather than losing hardness through the mass production effect?

evidence.quote: Can one take a sufficiently hard function with constant number of inputs and cook out of it a family of functions of high circuit complexity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C(f)$ denote the minimum number of gates in a Boolean circuit over the binary basis $B_2$ (the set of all two-input Boolean functions) that computes a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}$. It is known by counting that for every $k$ there exists a Boolean function $g:\{0,1\}^k\to\{0,1\}$ with $C(g) \ge (2^k/k)(1-o(1))$, but no explicit such $g$ is known for super-constant $k$.

Suppose one is given, as an oracle or fixed combinatorial object, a Boolean function $g:\{0,1\}^k\to\{0,1\}$ on a constant number $k$ of inputs whose circuit complexity $C(g)$ is as large as possible (i.e., close to $2^k/k$). The question is whether such a hard "seed" $g$ can be used to construct, in a systematic and uniform way, an explicit family $\{f_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\}_{n\ge 1}$ of Boolean functions such that $C(f_n)$ grows superlinearly (or even, ideally, matches the best known existential lower bounds up to constants) as $n\to\infty$.

More precisely: does there exist a polynomial-time (or otherwise effective) procedure that, given the truth table of any Boolean function $g$ on $k$ variables with $C(g)\ge c\cdot 2^k/k$ for some constant $c>0$, outputs a description of an $n$-variable Boolean function $f_n$ (for each $n$) such that $C(f_n) = \omega(n)$, avoiding the "mass production" phenomenon by which natural reductions from a $k$-input hard function only yield circuit lower bounds that vanish in $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: No general construction is known that converts a hard constant-arity Boolean function into an explicit family with high circuit complexity; proving superlinear lower bounds against unrestricted $B_2$-circuits remains a longstanding open problem in complexity theory, and the best known explicit lower bound is still of the form $(3+1/86)n - o(n)$ (Find–Golovnev–Hirsch–Kulikov 2016). The "mass production" obstruction described by Valiant remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Can one take a sufficiently hard function with constant number of inputs and cook out of it a family of functions of high circuit complexity?
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem about converting small hard functions into hard families.

status_evidence.title: A Better-Than-3n Lower Bound for the Circuit Complexity of an Explicit Function
status_evidence.snippet: We prove a (3+1/86)n - o(n) lower bound on the circuit complexity over the full binary basis for an explicit Boolean function.
status_evidence.claim: Best known explicit lower bound for general Boolean circuits is barely superlinear, indicating no general hardness amplification from constant-arity hard functions is known.
